div.head: I Cn 22
div.ab: And we lærað, þæt ælc Cristen man geleornige, þæt he huru cunne rihtne geleafan [⁊] ariht understandan ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credan geleornian.
And we lærað, þæt alc Crysten man geleornige, þæt he huru cunne rihtne geleafan ariht understanden ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credo geleornian.
We lærað, þæt ælc Cristen man geleornige, þæt he cunne huru rihtne geleafan ⁊ ariht understandan ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credan geleornian.
Et omnis Christianus addiscat, ut saltem sane fidei rectam intelligentiam habeat et sciat ‘Pater noster’ et ‘Credo in Deum’,
We lærað þæt ælc Cristen man geleornige þæt he cunne huru rihtne geleafan ariht understandan ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credan geleornian.
We enjoin that every Christian man apply himself until he can at least understand aright the true belief, and learn the Pater Noster and the Creed.
Und wir schreiben vor, dass jeder Christenmensch [so viel] lerne, dass er wenigstens das richtige Glaubensbekenntniss ordentlich verstehen und Pater noster und Credo lernen könne.
And we instruct that every Christian man learn [so much] that he can at least rightly understand the true faith, and learn the Pater noster and the Creed.
div.note: G's ‘⁊’ (compare B; ‘á’ compare Cons. ‘semper’) should be struck with A, Ld and Wulfstan (Liebermann). Liebermann compares the Canons of Edgar 22; Wulfstan p. 20.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
